question: Is my house eligible for solar panels?

confidence.text: Medium: planning.data and Camden disagree about an Article 4 direction; we follow Camden.

limitations: An Article 4 direction here has ended but still shows on planning.data.
The share of solar power used at home follows the MCS tables for 2,500 kWh a year (a typical home, Ofgem); your own pattern may differ.
Rules for England, demo data for London.
Roof size and yield come from 1 m LIDAR and PVGIS: an installer's survey confirms them.
solar.next_step: Get quotes from two or three MCS certified installers. If you want it in writing, apply to Camden for a lawful development certificate.

facts.value: Basements (A4Ba3, from 2016-10-03): Removes permitted development for basements across the whole borough. Planning data says made 3 Oct 2016; Camden says adopted 1 Jun 2017.

Hampstead Conservation Area (excl. Frognal Way) (various properties) (A4Ha1, from 2010-09-01): Front elevations, roofs facing a road, hard surfaces and boundary walls, including solar panels on a roof facing a road. Cancelled by Camden when A4Ha2 came into force on 9 Jun 2026.

Hampstead Conservation Area (excl. Frognal Way) Non-immediate Article 4 (A4Ha2, from 2026-06-09): Same as the old direction for front elevations, roofs facing a road, hard surfaces and boundary walls, but solar panels are no longer covered.
planning.data still lists A4Ha1 with no end date; the council ended it on 2026-06-09. Using the council's decision.
S, 4.6 kWp, about 4696 kWh a year
facts.source: PVGIS 5.2, EU Joint Research Centre via Zetaris; roof from EA LIDAR

rules.clause: GPDO Sch 2 Part 14 Class A, A.2(c)
rules.plain: On a pitched roof, panels may stand up to 20 cm proud of the roof and may not go above the ridge.

rules.clause: GPDO Sch 2 Part 14 Class A, A.2(e)
rules.plain: In a conservation area, panels may not go on a wall, balcony or roof enclosure that faces a road. The roof is fine.

lines.one: Your south roof slope (48°) has room for about 4.6 kWp, about 4,696 kWh a year.
lines.why: This house is not listed and sits in Hampstead Conservation Area (1968), where panels cannot go on a wall facing a road since your north wall faces Church Row. Roof slopes are fine, so the south slope can take them, but planning.data still lists Article 4 A4Ha1, which Camden ended on 9 Jun 2026, so we follow Camden.
lines.get: About 4.6 kWp on the south slope, about 4,696 kWh a year.
lines.cost: For 4.6 kWp: about £7,300 to £9,700 to install, worth about £400 to £810 a year for a home using 2,500 kWh a year (Ofgem's typical figure), so about 9 to 24 years to pay back. No VAT on panels until 31 Mar 2027.

challenges: One cost figure would hide how much prices vary. Check the national median against the London average before quoting a cost.
One share of solar power used at home would hide that it depends on who is home in the day. Ask the MCS tables for all three occupancy types, for this roof and a typical yearly use.
